<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3a78f8bf4e6c14b90e02f888429c7746bd7bc465 && git checkout 3a78f8bf4e6c14b90e02f888429c7746bd7bc465
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6 b02b3f8c16ea80da01d042242fd60bf83764f03b && git checkout -B drift-repro 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6 && git merge --no-ff b02b3f8c16ea80da01d042242fd60bf83764f03b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b02b3f8c16ea80da01d042242fd60bf83764f03b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22835's body and both of its comments (claim 6109766787, os-dev-report 6110648560); #15206's os-dev-report 6108953446 (finding 1) and PR #22833's contract review 6109504501 (③); PR #22862 (its body, its 9-file list, and the net diff against the merge base `eed637c09f`: 9 files, +325 / −38, equal to the file list, over the branch's three commits `fccd98aea0`, the merge `6e19243562` and `b02b3f8c16`); `.changeset/15206-reads-environment-only.md` on `origin/main` (unchanged since the merge base and untouched by this diff); the 41 check-runs and the one commit status on the head, read at 2026-10-11T15:51Z; `git merge-tree` of the head against `origin/main` at `55382dc02a`. Source at the head, read by symbol: `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` (`findEnvironmentRows`, `persistDatasourceRow`, `deleteDatasourceRow`, `loadDatasourceRows`, `loadDatasourceRow`, `restoreRuntimeDatasources`, `applyMetadataDoorWrite`, `convergePool`, `listDatasourceRecords`, `getDatasourceRecord`, `putDatasourceRecord`, `deleteDatasourceRecord`, `countBoundObjects`, `countBoundObjectsDiagnosed`, `DataEngineLike`), `datasource-admin-service.ts` (`createDatasource`, `updateDatasource`, `removeDatasource`), `legacy-organization-row.ts` and the `metadata-core` entry, objectql's `plugin.ts` (the hook, action and object-action binder reads) at the head and at the merge base, `metadata-protocol`'s `protocol.ts` (`reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows`, `loadMetaFromDb`'s per-type read, the by-name overlay read), the cli's `secret-reference-union.ts` (`readStoredDatasourceArtefacts`), the three edited test files and their doubles, the dogfood harness (`bootShowcase`, `BootOptions`, the `isolated` project's population), the ADR-0087 ledger entry `18.metadata-read-organization-scope-retired.ts` on `main` and at the merge base, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`'s `already-registered` rule, `.changeset/config.json` and `pre.json` on `main`, the ruleset's required contexts, the governed register in `check-governed-merges.mjs`, and the size job in `pr-automation.yml`. ⛔ Not the dispatch order, not the dispatching seat's conclusions. Nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run; the dev's gate run is read as the dev's report, never as a gate verdict. This is a `security` card: classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head, as read at 2026-10-11T15:51Z.** 41 check-runs: 31 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 5 `in_progress`, none red. Of the seven required contexts the ruleset names, six are `success`: `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (the rollup and 1/3 to 3/3), `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, and `TypeScript Type Check` (the rollup and its four legs — `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`, `workspace`). One has not concluded: `Test Core` — shard 1/6 is `success`, shards 2/6 to 6/6 are in progress, and no rollup has reported. This record judges what has concluded and does not wait; the landing's "every check green" is the seat's re-read at arming, outside this verdict. Also green: `Check Changeset` twice (no foreign changeset is modified — the pending note is not in the diff), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Spec property liveness`, `filter`, `Auto Label`, and the four claim and closing guards, twice each. Skipped by contract: `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate` (the pin is unchanged), `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and the `edited`-run twins of `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`. The one commit status, `Vercel`, is `success` (ignored build step). Not governed: none of the nine paths is a register row (`docs/adr/`, `.claude/`, `skills/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`); head repo is the base repo; draft; `auto_merge` unset; labels `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling`, no `skip-changeset`; `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: blocked` (the draft and the running checks, not a conflict).

1. **The census of the plugin's reads of stored `datasource` rows.** At the head `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` calls `engine.find` on `sys_metadata` in exactly one place, inside the new private `findEnvironmentRows` (type `datasource`, state `active`, one name when given, the explicit system context, then a `filter` dropping every row `isLegacyOrganizationRow` names); `findOne` appears nowhere in the file and leaves the private `DataEngineLike` slice. The helper's four callers are the whole population of stored-row reads: `loadDatasourceRows` (the boot restore, `restoreRuntimeDatasources`, whose own `engine.find` precondition matches); `loadDatasourceRow` (behind `applyMetadataDoorWrite`, the `/meta` door's datasource projection, and `convergePool`, cluster convergence); `persistDatasourceRow` (the existence probe behind `putDatasourceRecord`, which admin create and update reach); `deleteDatasourceRow` (the probe behind `deleteDatasourceRecord`, admin remove). The plugin's other reads — `listDatasourceRecords`, `getDatasourceRecord`, `countBoundObjects`, `countBoundObjectsDiagnosed` — read the MetadataService registry, never `sys_metadata`; they stop serving the legacy row because the restore no longer registers it (the dev's hypothesis 3, measured on the real boot and pinned on both doors). RIGHT, and complete within the package: no other file under `service-datasource/src` reads `sys_metadata` (`admin-routes.ts`, `datasource-admin-service.ts` and `plugin.ts` read the registry). **Outside the package**, one read of stored `datasource` rows exists and is rightly left outside the helper: `readStoredDatasourceArtefacts` in `packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts`, a driver-level find by type, deliberately unfiltered by state because it is the liveness sweep for secret handles (a handle a stored row still holds must not be collected); it serves nothing, and narrowing it would let a handle a legacy row at rest still carries be collected — the opposite of #22011 A. `metadata-protocol`'s own hydration and by-name overlay reads lower `organization_id: null` into the store (C5) and are environment-only already. `metadata-core/src/types.ts`, the spec's kernel schemas and the lint rules name the table without reading it.

2. **`findOne` → filtered `find` for the by-name reads.** Right, and necessary: a store-picked single row under a name held twice could be the legacy one while the environment's row exists. The unit pin inserts the legacy row FIRST under the shared name, so a first-match read would pick it, and the test double's `find` honours every `where` key by equality, so the organization work is done by the predicate alone. The `[#21913]` system-context pin's population count moves from one `find` plus four `findOne` to five `find` (two probes, the restore, convergence, the remove probe); its `expectAllSystem` assertion is unchanged, and the helper passes `SYSTEM_CTX` on the one call.

3. **The admin door's writes now.** Create under a legacy row's name: `createDatasource`'s existence check reads the registry, which no longer holds the row, and `persistDatasourceRow`'s probe finds no environment row, so an environment row is inserted; the legacy row is not touched. Update under such a name reaches the environment row only — `persistDatasourceRow`'s `update` is keyed on the id the filtered probe returned. Remove: `deleteDatasourceRow` deletes (or inactivates) only the environment row's id. Before, `deleteDatasourceRow`'s `findOne` by type, name and state could answer the legacy row and `engine.delete` took its id — the dev measured that remove DELETED the legacy row — and the same unfiltered probe in `persistDatasourceRow` could have rewritten one in place; both against #22011 A ("neither deleted nor rewritten"). Pinned twice: the unit case (update, remove and create under the shared name; the legacy row equals its inserted value at the end) and the dogfood case (an admin create and remove under the name write and remove an environment row of their own; a `/meta` save under the name is what the admin door then serves; the legacy row equals its planted bytes). RIGHT.

4. **The predicate move.** At the merge base `isLegacyOrganizationRow` was module-private in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`; at the head it is `packages/metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.ts`, exported through the package entry. The signature and the two-line body are byte-equal to the deleted private copy (`export` added, TSDoc extended); the truth table is pinned in `legacy-organization-row.test.ts` (an organization id is legacy; absent, `undefined`, `null`, the empty string, a `null` row and an `undefined` row are the environment's). objectql's three binder sites — the hook binder, the action binder and the object-action read — import it from `@objectstack/metadata-core` and are otherwise unchanged; `git grep` at the head finds no other definition in the tree. No new dependency edge: `objectql`, `service-datasource` and `metadata-protocol` already depend on `metadata-core` (`workspace:*`); `metadata-core` has no API-surface baseline to regenerate, and its `tsconfig` (`src/**/*`) compiles the new test under both of its `typecheck` programs. **The inline re-check in `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows`** (`metadata-protocol`): a filter of the same three comparisons (not `null`, not `undefined`, not the empty string) over the rows a driver that cannot lower the `$and` predicate hands back. It is the same truth table spelled a second time, not a second rule: it decides what a boot LOG LINE names, serves nothing, pre-dates this PR, is outside the claim's surface, and cannot make any read disagree about which rows are the environment's. Not a ground; a one-line import swap there is a follow-on for the seat if wanted (carrier: none, as the dev says). Also not a ground, and C5's own: `metadata-protocol`'s serving reads use the where-form `organization_id: null`, whose empty-string edge differs from the row-value form; the card's direction names the row-value form for this plugin, which is what landed, and it agrees with the binders and with the boot report.

5. **The boot report still names the row.** `protocol.ts` is not in the diff; `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows` is byte-unchanged from the merge base. Pinned: the dogfood premise case captures `console.warn` across the measured boot and asserts one `[metadata_org_scoped_unserved]` line naming the legacy row at its organization; the dev's before and after table reads the same. RIGHT.

6. **The pending note's sentence.** "A row stored organization-scoped by an earlier release is served by no read and loaded by no boot" — for `datasource` rows, now true at the head in the shipped compositions: the restore does not load it (item 1), neither door answers it by name and neither lists it (measured on a real boot and pinned), no pool opens from it, and the `/meta` projection and convergence cannot reach it; the one remaining reader, the cli's secret-handle sweep, serves nothing (item 1). The note is untouched by the diff (right: it is the sentence to make true, not to edit) and unchanged on `origin/main` since the merge base. The restore's `[#21922]` "code wins on collision" warning is untouched: `codeNames` is still read from the kernel's code-datasource set and the warning fires on the same condition, after the filter.

**Nothing is deleted or rewritten.** No added line calls a store write; the inserts, updates and deletes are the same calls as before, now keyed on an environment row's id only.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22835-datasource-reads-environment-only.md` (new, this PR's own): `@objectstack/service-datasource: minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-core: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: patch`; a `feat(...)!:` title; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; one FROM → TO row with the one-line fix (re-create through the admin door or save through the `/meta` door, or wait for the v18 ceremony); a closing line naming the new export. Each level judged: `service-datasource` — a BREAKING narrowing of a published door's answer, graded `minor` on the v18 prerelease line exactly as the pending note grades its own (`.changeset/pre.json` is `pre` with tag `next` on `main`; all three packages are in the fixed group; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`): right. `metadata-core` — a new public export is additive: `minor`, right. `objectql` — an import swap with no change in what it binds, a changed published artifact: `patch`, right (none is `skip-changeset`, which ruling D refuses for this class). **ADR-0087 marker** `not-required (already-registered metadata-read-organization-scope-retired)`: the id resolves on `main` — `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.metadata-read-organization-scope-retired.ts` and the pending note's `registered` marker — and both existed at the merge base `eed637c09f`, which is the gate's two-sided test for this category; `Check Changeset` is green twice. Honest: that entry's `replacement` already carries this change's prescription (a legacy organization-scoped row is served by no read; boot names each one; the v18 ceremony carries it; nothing is deleted or rewritten before it), the same one the changeset's row gives for a datasource row, so a new entry would duplicate a prescription the ledger holds. A precision note, not a ground: the entry's `surface` names `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s reads "and the boot hydration" and not the datasource-admin plugin; widening that wording is a spec edit with its regenerated artifacts, outside this diff. **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`** on PR body line 2, in the changeset and in the claim: right. No read refused today is admitted and no door answers more; a published door's answer narrows (the legacy row leaves both doors' answers and the pool). The new `metadata-core` export is not a widening in Clause-②'s sense — it admits no input and changes no door's answer — and it is carried by the `minor` level, which is the floor `yes` would set anyway; the closed pair admits one arm, and the narrowing is the breaking one. `no (widening)` would be malformed and `yes` would claim an admitted read that does not exist.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Deviations (a) to (h), each answered.** (a) file surface: the `metadata-core` module, entry export and truth-table test, and objectql's import swap — the claim names the move as part of this claim if the predicate moves to a package both sides depend on, which it does; stated in the report and the body; accepted (①4). (b) `DataEngineLike` drops `findOne` — a private type slice in the same file, now unused; the 21 doc pages the drift check lists are all reached through that `findOne` string literal in a `Pick`, so none documents what moved; `Flag docs affected by code changes` green; accepted. (c) `origin/main` merged into the branch at `6e19243562` before gating — four `main` commits, none in these packages; the net diff against the merge base `eed637c09f` equals the file list; accepted. (d) the changeset's three levels and the marker — ②; accepted. (e) line budget: +325 / −38, 363 changed lines against the 300 advisory, `size/m` by the labeler's bands; over by the 164-line real-boot pin, which is the shortest of the five datasource dogfood files at the head (its siblings run 178 to 323 lines) and is the pin the card asks for ("ablation-verified, on a real boot"); source is +59 / −36; advisory, not a gate; accepted. (f) zero label writes — right. (g) a temporary measurement copy of the dogfood file, run at the base and at the fix and deleted — nothing of it is in the diff; accepted. (h) the model-free trailer pair on both non-merge commits (the session trailer and the co-author trailer with no model identifier), the merge commit carrying none — what AGENTS.md requires; the harness reminder yields to it; right.

**The two out-of-scope findings.** (1) `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows`' inline re-check — judged in ①4: the same truth table, a log-line filter, not a second rule; carrier none is right. (2) no objectql test pins the hook and action binders' skip of a legacy organization row — true at the head (`protocol-meta.test.ts`'s ADR-0131 D6 cases cover the protocol reads, not the binders); the predicate itself is now pinned in `metadata-core`, the binder sites are unchanged, and the gap pre-dates this PR; carrier none, not a ground; the seat may file it against the objectql lane.

**`main` has moved.** `origin/main` is at `55382dc02a`, six commits past the merge base. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main b02b3f8c16` writes a tree with no conflict; no file `main` touched since the base is among the nine this PR touches; `.changeset/15206-reads-environment-only.md` is unchanged on `main` since the base. The nine paths are hand-written files, so no regenerated artifact is in the merge. The queue rebuilds on the merge ref; nothing asks for a pre-merge of `main`.

**Check-runs red or in progress.** Red: none. In progress at the reading: `Test Core` shards 2/6 to 6/6 (1/6 green), so the required `Test Core` context has not reported; the dev's own `vitest` runs of the three packages are the dev's report. The seat arms only on a re-read showing it green; a red there re-opens this record on the same head.

**For the seat at landing.** The PR's `Fixes #22835` is right (the card is this gap); #15206 is not closed by keyword and is closed by hand on MERGED, as its carry-over review 6109504501 left it open on exactly this sentence. The body's `+325 / −38 across 9 files` matches the diff. `skip-changeset` stays off.

**Verdict grounds, all on this head:** every read of a stored `datasource` row in the plugin goes through one helper carrying the one predicate C5's binders apply; the by-name reads are a filtered `find`; the writes under a legacy name touch an environment row only and the legacy row stays byte-equal; the predicate moved verbatim with its private copy deleted and no second definition in the tree; the boot report is untouched and still names the row; the pending note's sentence is now true for `datasource`; the three levels and the marker are right and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches the diff; no concluded check is red and no governed path is touched. The one required context still running, `Test Core`, is the seat's arming condition, not this record's.
